wst-unknown-notes-content\">\n<p><i>Mother Goose for Grownups</i> is an anthology of Carryl’s humorous light verse, published in 1900 by Harper &amp; Brothers, New York and London. These poems are parodies of the old traditional <i>Mother Goose</i> nursery rhymes. The volume was illustrated by Peter Newell and Gustave Verbeek. The dedication was a poem “<a href=\"/wiki/To_Constance\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"To Constance\">To Constance</a>”. The author added this foreword:\n</p>\n<blockquote><p>NOTE<br />I have pleasure in acknowledging the courteous permission of the editors to reprint in this form such of the following verses as were originally published in <i>Harper’s Magazine</i>, the <i>Saturday Evening Post</i>, and the <i>London Sketch</i>.<br />G. W. C.</p></blockquote>\n</div></div><div class=\"ws-noexport\" id=\"ws-data\" style=\"speak:none\"><span id=\"ws-article-id\">118551</span><span id=\"ws-title\">Mother Goose for Grownups</span><span
